Package frc.robot.commands

Class ShootWhenReady

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.commands.ShootWhenReady
public class ShootWhenReady extends Object
Waits until the robot is in a shoot-ready state, then runs the hopper to feed the ball.

What "Shoot Ready" Means

RobotStateMachine.isShootReady() returns true when all of the following are simultaneously true:
  • The shooter wheel speed is within AimParams.deltaOutput of the required speed for the current distance.
  • The hood angle is within AimParams.deltaPitch of the required angle for the current distance.
  • The turret is within AimParams.deltaYaw of the target yaw and is actively tracking (not just at home).
The condition is checked every robot loop (50 Hz) by polling the StateManager.shootReady trigger.

Command Sequence

   waitUntil(isShootReady)  â†’ hopper.startEnd(startAllMotors, stopAllMotors)
  1. The waitUntil step occupies zero subsystem requirements while waiting, so the turret and shooter (running under AimPrep) can continue operating in parallel on the same command group without a scheduling conflict.
  2. Once ready, startEnd starts both hopper motors and keeps them running until the command ends or is interrupted.

Why startEnd Instead of runOnce

startEnd guarantees that Hopper.stopAllMotors() is called in the command's end() method, regardless of whether the command ends normally or is interrupted. This is critical in autonomous: when a timed auto step expires, the scheduler interrupts the command and the hopper stops cleanly. With runOnce, the motors would start and then keep running into the next auto step because there is no cleanup.

Interaction with AimPrep

In teleop, this command is bound to the gunner's left bumper alongside AimPrep on the left trigger. The typical flow is:
  1. Hold left trigger â†’ AimPrep runs (turret tracks, shooter spins up).
  2. Press left bumper â†’ ShootWhenReady waits for ready condition, then feeds.
  3. Release left bumper â†’ hopper stops immediately via stopAllMotors.
  4. Release left trigger â†’ AimPrep ends, turret stops tracking, shooter stops.

In Autonomous

Named commands like "ShootFuel3s" wrap a parallel of AimPrep and this command inside a .withTimeout(3.0). When the timeout fires, both commands are interrupted, the hopper stops, and the path planner continues to the next segment.
